module purpose: neorv32_pwm decodes bus accesses into per-channel read and write enables for up to NUM_CHANNELS PWM channels. Each generated channel stores configuration from the write data bus, returns that configuration on reads, exports an enable request, and uses clkgen_i plus local counters to produce one PWM bit; the top level acknowledges accesses, combines channel readback, OR-reduces channel enable requests, and maps the channel bits into pwm_o.

use-case flows.value: per-channel access qualification from bus address, strobe, and read/write direction
per-channel enable, prescaler, polarity, clock-divider, and duty settings written from the bus data path into held registers
per-channel enable requests copied from channel enable settings and OR-reduced onto clkgen_en_o
per-channel divider count, tick generation, duty count, and PWM output update from stored settings and clkgen_i
stored channel configuration packed onto rdata_o, OR-combined into rdata_sum, and returned on the bus response data path when accessed
bus response, channel configuration, counters, and PWM outputs forced to their reset values while rstn_i is low

conceptual assets.concept: Per-channel bus access qualification -- which channel is selected and whether the access is a write or a read
conceptual assets.reasoning: The configure and read-out flows begin with the decode `sel(i) <= '1' when ...` and the qualified enables `we(i) <= sel(i) and bus_req_i.stb and bus_req_i.rw` and `re(i) <= sel(i) and bus_req_i.stb and not bus_req_i.rw` (lines 109-111). Lines 99-100 deliver these decisions to each generated channel, where `we_i` gates configuration writes (lines 183-188) and `re_i` gates readback (line 194). Integrity is established because a wrong selection or direction writes or reads the wrong channel. Availability is established conditionally: when the predicates of lines 109-111 hold, the corresponding channel-enable decision is produced and delivered. The bus request interface is a complete transport record, so the realized decision is reported on internal decode signals rather than on `bus_req_i` or its fields.

conceptual assets.concept: Per-channel PWM operating configuration -- the stored enable, prescaler, polarity, divider, and duty settings
conceptual assets.reasoning: For each generated channel in the loop at lines 93-112, `if (we_i = '1')` stores `cfg_en`, `cfg_prsc`, `cfg_pol`, `cfg_cdiv`, and `cfg_duty` from `wdata_i` (lines 183-188). The operate flow consumes these stored settings through `clkgen_en_o <= cfg_en` (line 197), the selected `clkgen_i` bit (line 214), the divider compare (line 215), and the PWM compare and polarity assignments (lines 231-234). The read-out flow packs the same stored fields onto `rdata_o` when `re_i = '1'` (line 194). Integrity is established because PWM generation, clock-enable requesting, and readback must follow these stored settings. Availability is established because the registers retain their values between writes and are reset to defined values on lines 176-181.

conceptual assets.concept: Combined channel-enable request -- the OR of generated channel enable requests exported on clkgen_en_o
conceptual assets.reasoning: Each generated channel copies its stored enable setting to its local request output with `clkgen_en_o <= cfg_en` (line 197), and the top level maps these requests to `ce(i)` (line 104) and drives `clkgen_en_o <= or_reduce_f(ce);` (line 121). Integrity is established because the exported enable decision must equal the OR of the generated channel requests. Availability is established because the output is continuously driven from the channel request path whenever channel enables are stored. The internal signal `ce` only carries sub-unit outputs to this reduction and is therefore not the structural reference.

conceptual assets.concept: Per-channel PWM sequencing state -- the divider count, divider-match tick, and duty counter that advance output timing
conceptual assets.reasoning: The runtime operate flow updates `cnt_cdiv` and `cnt_tick` when the selected `clkgen_i` bit is asserted: `cnt_cdiv` resets on equality with `cfg_cdiv` or increments otherwise, and `cnt_tick` is raised on the equality case (lines 214-219). `cnt_duty` resets when disabled and increments on `cnt_tick` (lines 224-227). The output compare then uses this state at lines 231-234. Integrity is established because correct PWM generation depends on the correctness of this internal timing state and tick decision. Availability is established under the RTL-visible conditions `cfg_en = '1'` and the selected `clkgen_i` bit being asserted, because these state elements update and retain their values between edges.

conceptual assets.concept: Generated PWM output bits -- the values placed on each channel output and assembled into the top-level pwm_o vector
conceptual assets.reasoning: Each generated channel drives its output by the compare and polarity rule `if (cfg_en = '0') or (unsigned(cnt_duty) >= unsigned(cfg_duty)) then pwm_o <= cfg_pol; else pwm_o <= not cfg_pol; end if;` (lines 231-234). The top level then clears the whole output vector and copies the generated channel bits into `pwm_o(pwm'range)` (lines 116-117), leaving unused high bits at zero. Integrity is established because the delivered output bits must follow this rule. Availability is established because the channel output is reset to a defined value on line 207 and the top-level vector is always driven by the process of lines 114-117.
